tools.name: alignment_check
tools.description: Record what the agent understood, its confidence, and any human correction. Measures the Intelligent Distance gap.

tools.name: awareness_update
tools.description: Add insights to the awareness system. Call at end of session. New insights are merged with existing ones (strengthening confirmed patterns) or added (demoting least-relevant if over 20). Also updates the cross-project insights index.

trajectory.description: Where is the work heading? One line.

blind_spots.description: What might matter but hasn't been explored?

identity.description: Update user identity (only on first use or major change)

tools.poisoning_detail: Tool may exhibit different behavior after initial uses (sleeper pattern). Matched pattern in tool 'awareness_update': 'on first use'

tools.name: check_action
tools.description: Call BEFORE any non-trivial action (publish, push, deploy, schema change, file delete, send message, modify config). Pass a one-sentence description of what you're about to do. Returns matching behavior rules + active corrections + high-salience insights — a short list of memory items that would otherwise be re-derived or forgotten. Deterministic keyword match (no LLM call), runs in <50 ms. If `warning` is non-null, READ IT before acting.

action_description.description: What you're about to do — one sentence, specific (e.g. 'publish agent-recall-mcp@3.5.0 to npm').

min_overlap.description: Minimum overlapping tokens between action and memory item. Default 2 (signal floor for relevance). Lower to 1 for permissive matching, raise to 3+ for strict.

tools.name: check
tools.description: [MID-SESSION — safe any time; for alignment, before risky decisions] Use when the user asks to validate understanding, verify alignment, or check if their interpretation matches the human's intent. Also call BEFORE a high-risk action — publish, deploy, delete, credential exposure, external send/message, or any other irreversible write — passing `action_description` (one sentence, what you're about to do). Returns matching corrections/rules/insights plus a `verdict`: `blocked` means an authoritative correction OVERRIDES the plan — read it before proceeding. To RECORD a durable human correction, pass `human_correction` as the STRUCTURED object {rule, why, applies_when} — a plain string is only STAGED for later review, never activated. ON THIS SERVER agents can only PROPOSE corrections: every human_correction, including the structured form and pending_id, is staged for the owner's confirmation. You cannot activate, promote or confirm one; tell the user it is waiting for the owner.

goal.description: The goal or decision question you're checking alignment on. Required for alignment checks; optional when recording a pure decision trail (prior/posterior/evidence).

understanding.description: Alias for goal — use when saying 'check my understanding: X'. Provide either goal or understanding.

confidence.description: How confident you are. Defaults to medium.

human_correction.description: After human responds: what they actually wanted. Pass the OBJECT form {rule, why, applies_when} to activate a durable correction; a plain string is only staged for review.

delta.description: The gap between your understanding and reality (or 'none').

prior.description: Initial probability estimate (0-1). Start of Bayesian decision trail.

evidence.description: Evidence collected since prior. Each entry shifts probability.

outcome.description: Final decision result: 'confirmed', 'rejected', 'partial', or free text. Triggers decision trail persistence.

decision_id.description: Link multiple check calls to the same decision. Auto-generated if not provided.

action_description.description: What you're about to DO, one sentence — pass this before publish/deploy/delete/credential/external-send/irreversible-write actions. Returns matching corrections/rules/insights on the result's `action_check` field, with `verdict: "blocked"` when an authoritative correction overrides the plan.

Start a new AgentRecall session for project "{project}".
for project "{project}"
1. Call `session_start()` to load project context — identity, insights, active palace rooms, cross-project matches, watch_for warnings.

2. Call `recall("{task}")` to surface task-specific past knowledge.

prompts.name: arsave
prompts.description: Save everything from this session — journal, palace consolidation, awareness insights. Call at the end of every productive session.
message_literals: user
text

Save this session to AgentRecall.
Session summary: "{args.summary}"
1. Review what happened: decisions made, work completed, corrections received, blockers identified.

2. If any corrections happened (human said 'no not that', 'I meant X'), call `check()` with `human_correction` as a STRUCTURED object {rule, why, applies_when} (one imperative rule sentence + evidence + context keywords) plus `delta` — a plain string is only staged for review, never activated.
3. Call `session_end()` with:
- `summary`: 2-3 sentence session summary
- `insights`: 1-3 reusable learnings (not 'fixed a bug' but 'API returns null when session expires — always null-check')
- `trajectory`: where the work is heading next
4. Verify: call `recall()` with a key decision from today to confirm it was saved.
Do NOT push to git. All data is local-first. Only push if the user explicitly asks.

prompts.name: arsaveall
prompts.description: Scan all of today's sessions across all projects and save them in one consolidated pass. Use when multiple agents ran in parallel.
message_literals: user
text
Batch save all of today's sessions across all projects.
1. Scan: find all journal and capture-log files from today across all projects in ~/.agent-recall/projects/.
2. For each project with unsaved sessions: call `session_end()` with a merged summary covering all sessions.
3. Deduplicate insights across projects — don't save the same insight twice.
4. Call `awareness_update()` once with cross-project insights.
5. Report what was saved: projects, sessions merged, insights added.
Each parallel session writes to its own file (session-ID scoped), so there are no conflicts.
Do NOT push to git unless the user explicitly asks.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
